evidence: The survivor precomputes "allowed pairs for colors 1..3" and then solves the resulting constraint graph; the defeated solutions likewise use "Try colors 0,1,2" and brute-force "3^n" assignments.
affordance_in_statement: Every installation i must be assigned exactly one frequency multiplier c_i ∈ {1, 2, 3}, and for every interacting pair P(u, v) = c_u^2 + c_u c_v + c_v^2 must not be a multiple of 3.
removal_suggestion: Do not expose the constraint as a small fixed three-value coloring relation in the statement; present the acoustic compatibility test through an indirectly defined evaluation procedure or scenario-specific transformation, while preserving the same mathematical condition and examples.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that the modular quadratic condition is equivalent to requiring different colors on every edge, then applies a graph 3-coloring search with precomputed allowed pairs.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The explicit domain {1, 2, 3} together with P(u, v) = c_u^2 + c_u c_v + c_v^2 modulo 3.

common_affordance: The modular constraint collapses exactly to ordinary proper 3-coloring of the interaction graph.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Uses a fixed vertex-order recursive 3-coloring search without a strong branching heuristic, so it encounters exponential blowups on hard n=40 instances.
Enumerates all 3^n assignments instead of using graph-coloring propagation or search heuristics, causing TLE.

recommended_edit: Re-present the compatibility rule indirectly rather than as the visibly simple modulo-3 quadratic over the three explicit values, so that the immediate reduction to proper 3-coloring is not exposed.
regression_risk: A superficial rewording may not defeat a capable solver that performs the same modular derivation; because the reduction is intrinsic to the current mathematical task, any fully reliable removal would require changing the constraint itself.
